messages.subject: Re: Installation Problems in rstan 2.7 under (Arch) Linux: No file or directory
parts:
We have fixed it but a better temporary fix (if your .Rprofile prints stuff to the screen) is to temporarily set R_PROFILE_USER to a non-existent file if you are building the package from source (i.e. not on Windows or Mac typically).

Sys.unsetenv("R_PROFILE_USER")
install.packages("rstan", dependencies = TRUE)

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installation Problems in rstan 2.7 under (Arch) Linux: No file or directory
parts:
On Wednesday, July 22, 2015 at 2:09:54 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
That was the magic incantation that worked for me on Mac OS X.
Like one of the users I was trying to help install, we both just
thought

> install.packages("rstan")

was going to work because we already had working C++ toolchains from
previous versions of RStan.  But it failed to find the Stan headers when
compiling, so I had to use Ben's suggestion below after following the first
piece of config advice here under Configuration:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started
You have to call
install.packages("rstan", dependencies = TRUE)

in order to get the packages (such as StanHeaders) listed under Suggests, which are actually required but not listed under Depends because they do not need to be loaded into R's memory (only available on the hard disk).

Ben

messages.author: c4d395346152354a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installation Problems in rstan 2.7 under (Arch) Linux: No file or directory
parts:
From the docs, the dependencies parameter in install.packages is defaulted to dependencies = NA.
So it seems that if you don’t have the nice button checked off in Rstudio you need to have the dependencies flag to True.

My issue seemed to be from the build/makefile, it was searching for StanHeaders in the wrong directory.

Apparently StanHeaders changed between the 2.6 and 2.7 release?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installation Problems in rstan 2.7 under (Arch) Linux: No file or directory
parts:
On Wednesday, July 22, 2015 at 2:36:08 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> On Jul 22, 2015, at 2:32 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ...

> There is no fix for the dependencies thing; you have to call install.packages("rstan") with dependencies = TRUE like the Wiki page says.

Does this mean that install.packages("rstan") will never
work on its own?

It would work for something like a hypothetical rstan 2.7.0-2 release iff the user has already installed rstan 2.7.0-1 with its dependencies, since 2.7.0-2 will be compatible with StanHeaders 2.7.0. We can maybe add to the startup banner if StanHeaders is not found. But people on Windows / Mac need to get into the habit of specifying dependencies = TRUE when they install or upgrade rstan.

Ben
